- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 7–10 days to catch mean reversion.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a 1–3% downward bias for days 1–7, then adjust to mean-reversion trend.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 1.00 → 0.33 → 1.00), model tends to mispredict direction; use sentiment-weighted moving average for smoothing.
